body: An additional thing to note is that differences in the lightmap scale when importing and auto generating UV2 in Godot, can effect how close the panels are, and if the scale is incorrect edge bleeds may overlap. Increasing the Lightmap Size Hint values corrects this, lightmaps could benefit from an import value that relates to pixels per metre or the desired texture sheet size for a given unwrap (to allow artists to import via Blender and guarantee the same pixel density)

A couple more examples with a solidified mesh using both sides of faces (internal faces of the mesh are also lightmapped, this is unpreventable as shadow models must have the same number of faces/vertexes as source model).

Here is 6 directional lights, one on each axis. Texels on incorrectly wound vertexes seem to not hit any occluders.
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/987cbf40-02d2-4cd2-ac1e-b380430a40af)

And with omni lights, the default import value of 0.2, and a LightmapGI Texel Scale of 0.5
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e5fc4586-f941-4f67-be20-01755627f84f)

Only texels on surfaces that would be in the path of the light, but fall on the edge have leaks.
Note that if I use the default values of 0.2 on Generate Lightmap UV2 Texel Size and 1.0 on LightmapGI Texel Scale, black bars on edges still appear, but leaks only appear on the internal parts of the solidified hull.

My initial supposition might not be correct, it may not be the edge bleed generator. Its appears to be related to winding order/orientation of the face on the UV canvas. 

Its provable that incorrectly lit texels must be in the path of the light and on the edge of UV2. Its provable that changing the face orientation in UV2 alleviates the issue, however it is not symmetric and may be based on winding order.

It's likely that once its fixed, single planes will occlude correctly and solidified hulls wont be needed 🤞
